q: Human eye consists of sense organs which are capable of receiving visual images and sending the information to the ____.
e: The eye receives visual images and sends them to the brain along the optic nerve. The retinal image is real, inverted and smaller than the object. The brain interprets that picture as upright.

q: Since the eyelid opens and closes the eye, it is similar to the lens ____ of the camera.
e: A camera forms a real inverted image with a convex lens and records it on film or a pixel sensor. The diaphragm sets how much light; the shutter sets how long. The focusing ring sets lens-to-film distance for sharpness.

q: The front portion of the eye is covered by a tough, transparent membrane called the ____.

q: Farsightedness is a defect of vision in which distant objects are seen clearly, but objects nearby are ____.
e: Farsightedness, hyperopia: distant objects are clear, nearby ones are blurry. Near rays meet behind the retina, so a converging convex lens is the correction. A diverging lens is the myopia tool, not this one.

q: Nearsightedness is a defect of vision in which near objects are seen clearly, but objects far away are ____.
e: Nearsightedness, myopia: near objects are clear, distant ones are blurry. Distant rays meet in front of the retina, so a diverging concave lens is the correction. A convex lens would add even more convergence.

e: Least distance of distinct vision is about 25 cm for a normal eye. Nearer than that, the lens cannot bulge enough. The far point for normal vision is infinity.
